newsitem.title: USA: CBOT January soy complex expiry seen quiet - trade.
newsitem.headline: CBOT January soy complex expiry seen quiet - trade.

text.p: Wednesday's expiration of Chicago Board of Trade January soy complex futures was expected to be quiet after funds and commercials liquidated positions on Tuesday, traders said.
"We lost half of what we had (open interest) yesterday," one trader said. "It shouldn't be a crisis situation."
The January soybean, soymeal and soyoil contracts expire Wednesday at 1201 CST/1801 GMT.
Traders expected a calm session after open interest dropped sharply, reflecting Tuesday's active trade.
Open interest in January soybeans was estimated at 2,500 contracts after Tuesday's session, down 2,215 contracts from Monday, CBOT reported.
January soymeal open interest was pegged at 468 lots, down 845 lots on Tuesday. Soyoil was estimated at 645 lots, down 583 lots on Tuesday.
Light deliveries in soymeal suggested a firm finish in that market, traders said. Eight lots were delivered on Wednesday, which one trader said was an insignificant amount.
"If you're short the meal, you've got a problem," another pit source said, but added, "I look for the major portion of this to get rectified today."
At 1000 CST, January soymeal was up $1.80 per ton at $248.50 a ton.

Traders noted Farmers Commodity Corp sold 150 lots January soymeal during Tuesday's session. Cargill Inc and E.D. and F. Man International reportedly bought 50 lots January while LIT America bought 150 lots January, traders said.
Traders speculated that January soybeans would also end firm after commercial interests stopped all 470,000 bushels posted for delivery on Wednesday.
"Cargill stopping the beans should keep the January strong on expiration," one floor trader said.

Traders said ADM bought 500,000 bushels January soybeans on Tuesday and sold 200,000 bushels. Produce Grain and Prudential Securities each reportedly spread 300,000 bushels January/March, and Smith Barney spread 300,000 March/January.
Spreads were also active Tuesday as ADM reportedly spread 150 lots March/January. Refco Inc spread 50 lots January/May and Tenco spread 75 lots January/March, traders said.
January soyoil futures will likely finish weak, under a bearish tone set by heavy deliveries this month. There were 350 lots of soyoil posted for delivery on Wednesday.
ADM reportedly sold 50 lots January soyoil during Tuesday's session, traders said.
